title: Asymptotic Properties of Nearest Neighbor Rules Using Edited Data
ndnote: Theoretical paper; no empirical datasets, only analytic risk calculations for assumed two-class 1-D populations
srcdet: Asymptotic risk computed analytically for 1-D normal densities: N(0,1) vs N(1,1); N(0,1) vs N(0,4); N(-2,1) vs N(2,1).
crit: Populations were chosen to give closed-form or numerically computable Bayes and NN risks with increasing class separation and a variance difference. Selection is analytical and unrelated to benchmark practice.
irnote: Not applicable; equal priors are presumably assumed.
specnote: Like Tomek links, ENN entered the imbalance literature only later as a cleaning primitive. The overlapping normal populations give a nonzero Bayes risk, which is the conceptual root of the class-overlap idea.
prep: 3-NN editing followed by 1-NN classification.
ev: Fig. 2 compares the asymptotic performance of the nearest neighbor rules with the performance of Bayes' rule when population one is a normal distribution centered at 0 with variance 1

title: Two Modifications of CNN
ndnote: One illustrative 2-D synthetic example only; no benchmark datasets
srcdet: Design set of 400 samples (200 per class) with uniform distributions in two dimensions and an irregular boundary, taken from an earlier reference.
crit: The example was chosen only to illustrate how the proposed modifications retain points near the class boundary compared with CNN. It is a toy 2-D case and no benchmark rationale is given. Imbalance is not the topic of the paper.
irnote: Balanced, 200 vs 200.
specnote: Included for completeness as the origin of Tomek links, which later became an imbalance cleaning primitive. The original paper has no imbalanced evaluation at all, which is worth noting when the survey traces lineage.
prep: None stated.
ev: For example illustration the original set consists of 200 samples in each of two classes with uniform distributions

title: A Decision-Theoretic Generalization of On-Line Learning and an Application to Boosting
ndnote: Theoretical paper with no experimental dataset section; it mentions only some initial experiments on unnamed real-world problems
srcdet: No datasets. OCR handwritten digits appear only as a hypothetical motivating example for multi-class and multi-label boosting.
crit: Not applicable. The paper has no empirical evaluation section; its contribution is a decision-theoretic generalisation of on-line learning and the AdaBoost bounds. It is relevant to this survey only as the base algorithm for SMOTEBoost, RUSBoost, RAMOBoost and RBBoost.
specnote: Included as a lineage node only. It has no data and is not an imbalance paper, so it should be cited in the method section rather than counted in the Data section statistics.
ev: Some initial experiments using AdaBoost on real-world problems conducted by ourselves and Drucker and Cortes indicate that AdaBoost tends not to overfit

title: Addressing the Curse of Imbalanced Training Sets: One-Sided Selection
ndnote: 2 oil-spill variants + 2 sleep EEG files + 3 binarised UCI sets
srcdet: Oil-spill satellite radar (oil1, oil2) and EEG sleep data from the authors' own projects; glass, vowels, vehicles from UCI.
crit: First group comes from the two projects that motivated the work and are called very difficult tasks with insufficient and many irrelevant attributes. UCI sets were added following the common practice of the ML community so other researchers can replicate and double-check results. Multiclass UCI sets were turned into two-class tasks by choosing one class as positive.
irnote: Not reported as IR; computed from Table 3 (veh1 676/168=4.0; oil1 480/24=20).
specnote: Positives are extremely scarce in the oil-spill sets (about two dozen positives vs hundreds of look-alikes). Stresses noisy, borderline and redundant majority examples; uses g-mean rather than accuracy.
prep: All attributes continuous. UCI multiclass binarised (glass c7, vowels c0, vehicles c1). Stratified k-fold CV, k = 4 to 8. Examples randomly discarded in g7 and veh1 to equalise fold proportions. 1-NN and C4.5.
ev: experimented with some data files from the UCI repository so that other researchers can replicate the experiments and double-check our results.

title: Machine Learning for the Detection of Oil Spills in Satellite Radar Images
ndnote: Single proprietary oil-spill dataset from 9 SAR images (9 batches), 937 dark-region examples
srcdet: Feature vectors of dark regions from 9 SAR radar images of the Juan de Fuca strait, labelled by a human expert. Not public.
crit: Data come directly from the application (oil-spill detection system). The authors acquired only images that contain oil slicks to maximise the number of positives, and acknowledge this makes the class distribution differ from deployment. An application case study, not a benchmark selection.
irnote: 41 positives vs 896 negatives, about 96% majority.
specnote: First paper to present the oil-spill dataset that later became a standard imbalanced benchmark (reused by SMOTE and LS). Emphasises examples grouped in batches (images) and the scarcity of positives.
prep: Image processing normalises the radar images and extracts 49 features per dark region. 10-fold CV (5 runs) plus a leave-one-batch-out protocol that tests on unseen images. g-mean and ROC.
ev: The nine images (batches) contain a total of 41 positive examples and 896 negative examples

title: SMOTE: Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique
ndnote: Pima, Phoneme, Adult, E-state, Satimage, Forest Cover, Oil, Mammography, Can. Satimage and Forest Cover reduced to two classes.
srcdet: UCI (Pima, Adult, Satimage, Forest Cover), ELENA (Phoneme), NCI Yeast AntiCancer E-state descriptors, Oil from Kubat et al. 1998, Mammography (Woods et al. 1993), Can from a Sandia crash-simulation mesh.
crit: Datasets were chosen to vary extensively in size and class proportions, thus offering different domains for SMOTE, and are listed in order of increasing imbalance. The system works for two-class problems, so multiclass sets were reduced to two classes. Several sets had been used by earlier imbalance work (Satimage collapsed as in Provost et al.; Oil from Kubat et al.).
irnote: Computed from stated class counts: Pima 1.87 to Can 435512/8360 = 52.1.
specnote: Widest range of scale and imbalance among the early papers (768 to about 444k samples). Includes real-world non-UCI data (E-state, Mammography, Can) and Adult with 6 continuous and 8 nominal features, which motivates SMOTE-NC.
prep: Forest Cover reduced to two classes (Ponderosa Pine vs Cottonwood/Willow). Satimage smallest class as minority, rest collapsed. Adult continuous features only for SMOTE. ROC analysis with C4.5, Ripper and Naive Bayes; 10-fold CV.
ev: We experimented on nine different datasets. These datasets vary extensively in their size and class proportions, thus offering different domains for SMOTE.

title: SMOTEBoost: Improving Prediction of the Minority Class in Boosting
ndnote: KDDCup-99 intrusion (5 classes, analysed per minority class U2R and R2L), Mammography, Satimage and Phoneme
srcdet: KDDCup-99 (UCI KDD archive); Mammography (Chawla et al. 2002); Satimage (UCI, smallest class as minority); Phoneme (ELENA).
crit: Datasets from several domains chosen to give different degrees of imbalance and different sizes, from highly imbalanced (KDD U2R, mammography) to moderately imbalanced (phoneme). KDDCup-99 was re-sampled (train and test merged, 69980 connections sampled only from the majority classes, then split into equal train and test) so that train and test distributions match.
irnote: Derived from Table 2: Phoneme 2.41, Satimage 9.28, Mammography 42.0, KDD Normal vs U2R about 128.
specnote: One of the earliest papers to make the train/test distribution match an explicit design decision rather than an afterthought. Only minority-class precision, recall and F-value are reported.
prep: 10-fold CV except KDDCup which uses a separate test set. RIPPER base learner; SMOTE amount 100 to 500%; 25 boosting iterations.
ev: Our experiments were performed on the four data sets summarized in Table 2.

title: A Study of the Behavior of Several Methods for Balancing Machine Learning Training Data
ndnote: Text says thirteen UCI sets; Table 3 has 15 rows because Splice and Letter each give two binary variants
srcdet: All from UCI: Pima, German, Post-operative, Haberman, Splice, Vehicle, Letter, New-thyroid, E.coli, Satimage, Flag, Glass, Nursery.
crit: The authors selected thirteen data sets from UCI which have different degrees of imbalance. Multiclass sets were turned into two-class problems (one class or a group of classes as minority). The choice is tied to their hypothesis that imbalance combined with class overlap and few positive examples causes the difficulty.
irnote: Computed from Table 3 class percentages (Pima 1.88 to Nursery 38.2).
specnote: Broad UCI selection spanning minority share from about 2.5% to 35% and sizes from 90 to 20000. Mixed quantitative and qualitative attributes. Used to show imbalance alone does not hurt AUC, but overlap plus few positives does.
prep: Multiclass binarised (Satimage c4 vs rest, Vehicle van vs rest, Letter-vowel, Letter-a). 10-fold CV, C4.5 release 8 pruned and unpruned, AUC. Over-sampling balanced classes fully.
ev: we have selected thirteen data sets from UCI which have different degrees of imbalance.

title: Borderline-SMOTE: A New Over-Sampling Method in Imbalanced Data Sets Learning
ndnote: 1 simulated (Circle) + 3 UCI (Pima, Satimage, Haberman)
srcdet: Simulated 2-D Circle dataset plus UCI Pima, Satimage and Haberman.
crit: Not stated explicitly. The Circle set is simulated to illustrate how borderline examples are found and over-sampled. UCI sets are all-quantitative and span minority proportions of about 10% to 35%. Only two-class problems are studied, so Satimage was binarised.
irnote: Computed from the minority percentages in Table 2 (Pima 34.77% to Circle 6.25%).
specnote: Very small evaluation (4 sets) including a synthetic 2-D illustrative set. Imbalance is moderate; only minority-class TP rate and F-value are reported.
prep: Satimage class 4 as minority, rest majority. 10-fold CV averaged over three runs. C4.5.
ev: The four data sets used in our experiments are shown in Table 2. Among the four data sets, Circle is our simulated data set and the others are from UCI

title: Combating Imbalance in Network Intrusion Datasets
ndnote: Two proprietary Notre Dame network-traffic datasets: Packets and Destinations
srcdet: Real campus traffic from the University of Notre Dame (summer 2004), labelled with SNORT alerts; per-packet and per-destination views.
crit: The authors built their own datasets because the DARPA'98 benchmark was criticised for synthetic normal traffic that is not representative of modern traffic. The two views give datasets with different features and class distributions; Packets has the less favourable imbalance and is expected to give a more compelling case for SMOTE.
irnote: Computed from Table I: Destinations 3933/147 = 26.8; Packets 344514/2106 = 163.6.
specnote: Network intrusion detection. SNORT multi-label alerts collapsed to intrusive vs non-intrusive. Destinations has a very small minority (147 alerts) forming a single compact cluster, which limits Cluster-SMOTE there.
prep: Packets: stratified 75/25 split. Destinations: 10-fold CV. Payload summarised as character-class percentages. Nominal features handled with a VDM-based distance. RIPPER with ROC analysis.
ev: We evaluate our approaches on two intrusion datasets, destination and actual packets based, constructed from actual Notre Dame traffic

title: On Multi-Class Cost-Sensitive Learning (conference version)
ndnote: 14 UCI + 6 synthetic; the first 10 are balanced and the other 10 imbalanced. Pure imbalance experiments use only the 10 imbalanced sets.
srcdet: 14 UCI sets. 6 synthetic sets (syn-a to syn-f): 2 attributes, 3 or 5 classes, normal distributions with random mean and std in [0,10].
crit: Chosen to cover multi-class problems both without and with class imbalance, so cost-sensitive rescaling can be tested on balanced and imbalanced data. Cost matrices are generated randomly. For imbalanced sets the cost of misclassifying the smallest class into the largest is forced to be the largest, because otherwise standard learners already do well. Minority and majority are not defined explicitly: imbalance is simply the raw class-size distribution.
irnote: IR not tabulated. Derived from Table 2 class distributions as max/min: balanced sets 1.0; page 4913/28 = 175.5; ann about 40.
specnote: The experimental focus is cost matrices (consistent vs inconsistent), not data difficulty. Several sets are categorical (car, solarflare2, splice).
prep: Instance weighting with C4.5. 10 x 10-fold CV with random cost matrices; MAUC used for pure imbalance.
ev: Twenty multi-class data sets are used in the experiments, where the first ten data sets are without class imbalance while the remaining ten are imbalanced. There are 14 UCI data sets and 6 synthetic data sets.
ds_note: Synthetic sets are named individually (2 attributes, 3 or 5 classes, random normal distributions), so they are listed rather than aggregated. First 10 rows balanced, last 10 imbalanced - a deliberate design, not an accident.

title: Local Decomposition for Rare Class Analysis
ndnote: 14 sets in Table 2 (8 UCI, 2 document, 4 LIBSVM) plus KDD-Cup'99 used to build two binary rare-class sets
srcdet: UCI (breast-w, pima, letter, optdigits, page-blocks, pendigits, satimage, vowel); documents k1b (WebACE) and la12 (TREC-5); LIBSVM (fourclass, german.numer, splice, SVMguide1); KDD-Cup'99.
crit: The authors used a number of benchmark data sets obtained from different application domains and report the coefficient of variation of class sizes to describe imbalance. For rare-class tests, binary sets were turned into imbalanced ones by randomly sampling the small class. Multiclass sets with different CV test COG on naturally imbalanced multiclass data, and balanced sets test whether COG also helps there.
irnote: Imbalance reported as CV of class sizes, not IR. Computed max/min: vowel 1.0; page-blocks 175.5; r2l binary 437.7.
specnote: Covers both binary and multiclass data including very high-dimensional text (k1b 21839 and la12 31472 features). Rare classes are artificially constructed by sampling the small class.
prep: 70/30 stratified split where no split is given. Documents: stop-list removal, Porter stemming, K-means with cosine similarity. 16 breast-w instances with missing data removed. KDD'99 10% sample; probe and r2l binarised. SVM, BMR, C4.5, RIPPER.
ev: we used eight well-known benchmark data sets from UCI Repository. We also used high-dimensional document data sets and four binary data sets from the LIBSVM repository

title: ADASYN: Adaptive Synthetic Sampling Approach for Imbalanced Learning
ndnote: 5 UCI datasets in the main comparison plus one artificial Gaussian set for the beta sweep
srcdet: UCI: Vehicle, Pima, Vowel, Ionosphere, Abalone. Artificial multidimensional Gaussian data used only in Fig. 1.
crit: The authors wanted real-world two-class imbalanced problems, so they modified several UCI datasets according to various literary results from similar experiments, citing DataBoost-IM and Provost et al. Abalone classes (18 as minority vs 9 as majority) follow the DataBoost-IM suggestion. Datasets span different sizes, dimensionalities and imbalance levels.
irnote: Derived from Table 1: Ionosphere 1.79 to Abalone 689/42 = 16.4.
specnote: Classic small-UCI benchmark. Multiclass sets binarised by choosing one class as minority. Abalone subsampled to two classes (731 of 4177) with the discrete sex feature removed.
prep: Vehicle Van vs rest; Vowel first vowel vs rest; Abalone c18 vs c9; Ionosphere bad radar as minority. 100 random runs, half of each class for training. k=5, SMOTE N=200, beta=1, d_th=0.75; decision tree.
ev: We test our algorithm on various real-world machine learning data sets as summarized in Table 1. All these data sets are available from the UCI Machine Learning Repository.

title: Start Globally, Optimize Locally, Predict Globally: Improving Performance on Imbalanced Data
ndnote: 20 real-world and UCI datasets; 9 synthetic radial scenarios used only for motivation
srcdet: UCI (Breast-W, Letter, Page, Pendigits, Pima, Satimage, Segment, Mammography, Phoneme via ELENA, Oil); LIBSVM (FourClass, German.numer, Splice, SVMGuide1); biological sets (Boundary, Calmodulin, PhosS); E-State; Compustat; KDD'99 intrusion.
crit: A comprehensive evaluation using 20 real-world and UCI datasets. Sets come from different domains, mixed sizes (about 0.6k to 20k) and a wide range of minority proportions (0.7% to 36%). Several were taken from the SMOTE paper. The authors argue that data properties beyond class skew (overlap, density, modality) affect the optimal sampling level, so a diverse collection is needed.
irnote: Computed from the minority percentage in Table 2 (FourClass 36% to Intrusion 0.7%).
specnote: Largest and most diverse collection among the early papers. Also includes synthetic two-class radial datasets used to study how density and class overlap change optimal sampling levels. Oil is described as small and very noisy.
prep: Multiclass UCI sets converted to 2 classes (smallest class as minority; Letter all vowels). 5x2-fold CV with AUROC and an inner 5-fold CV wrapper. Compustat and Intrusion keep natural splits. C4.5 (unpruned, Laplace) and SVM.
ev: A comprehensive evaluation using 20 real-world and UCI datasets.

dsagg.label: motivation-only synthetic radial scenarios (Fig. 2 / Table 1)
dsagg.description: two-class radial sets at 50:1000 skew on a 3x3 grid of positive density (High/Medium/Low) x centroid separation (High/Medium/Low); referred to by (density, separation) pair labels, not by names; not part of the 20-set evaluation.

ds_note: Clean separation between a 9-scenario synthetic motivation study and a 20-set real evaluation, and the headline count covers only the latter. Spelling drifts between tables ('Breast-W' vs 'Breast-w', 'SVMGuide1' vs 'SVMguide1'). Compustat and Intrusion carry fixed train/test splits.

title: Cluster-based under-sampling approaches for imbalanced data distributions
ndnote: 2 real datasets plus a generated family of synthetic datasets DSiEjDk (2 to 16 clusters; noise 10/20, 30/40, 50/60 percent; ratios 2:1 to 72:1). The number of synthetic sets is not stated.
srcdet: Census-Income Database (UCI KDD Archive, 1994-95 US Census CPS) and a private bank Overdue Detection Database. Synthetic: 10000 samples, 5 numerical and 5 categorical attributes, clusters containing both classes, with injected noise.
crit: Synthetic data were generated to control the number of clusters, the imbalance ratio and the noise level (disordered samples and exceptional samples), simulating real-world data. The two real datasets are applications the authors describe as binary imbalanced problems, typical of fraud, credit and risk settings.
irnote: Synthetic ratios 2:1 to 72:1. Census about 3.0:1; Overdue train about 3.3:1, test about 3.7:1 (computed).
specnote: The synthetic generator injects disordered samples (a class lying in the other class's area, that is label noise or overlap) and exceptional samples (irregular outliers) at levels up to 50 and 60 percent, an unusually explicit noise-control design for 2009.
prep: Census-Income: incomplete records removed, 80/20 split. Overdue: temporal split (train Nov-2004, test Dec-2004). Continuous attributes min-max normalised; categorical distance 0/1; k-means clustering.
ev: The total number of samples after cleaning the incomplete data is 30,162, including 22,654 majority class samples and 7508 minority class samples

title: Exploratory Undersampling for Class-Imbalance Learning
ndnote: 16 UCI datasets. Table II is now recovered, including the explicit target class used to binarise each multi-class source.
srcdet: UCI repository: abalone, balance, car, cmc, haberman, housing, ionosphere, letter, mf-morph, mf-zernike, phoneme, pima, satimage, vehicle, wdbc, wpbc. Attribute types are given per dataset as binary, nominal or continuous.
crit: 16 UCI datasets with various sizes and imbalance levels. For each dataset one target class is the minority class and all the others are merged into the majority class, and Table II publishes that target explicitly (abalone Ring=7, car acc, cmc class 2, housing target in [20,23], letter A, satimage class 4, vehicle opel, wdbc malignant, wpbc recur). Datasets are split post hoc into 6 easy tasks (AdaBoost AUC above 0.95) and 10 hard tasks to show where imbalance handling matters.
irnote: Ratio column of Table II: wdbc 1.7 at the low end, letter 24.3 at the high end, consistent with the statement that the imbalance level happens to be lower than 40.
specnote: One of the few papers that publishes the binarisation target for every dataset, which makes the benchmark exactly reproducible. It also splits the benchmark post hoc into easy and hard tasks by baseline AUC, a sharper diagnostic than IR alone. Imbalance is mild by the standards of this corpus, never exceeding 24.3.
prep: Stratified 10-fold CV; each fold repeated 10 times; whole CV repeated 5 times; CART weak learners, 40 iterations; SMOTE-NC for nominal attributes; AUC, F-measure, G-mean.
ev: We tested the proposed methods on 16 UCI data sets. Information about these data sets is summarized in Table II.

title: Safe-Level-SMOTE for Handling the Class Imbalanced Problem
ndnote: Only two UCI datasets (Satimage, Haberman); smallest benchmark in the corpus
srcdet: UCI Satimage (class 4 as minority, rest merged) and Haberman.
crit: Not stated beyond using two quantitative datasets from UCI, that is numeric attributes only (nominal attributes listed as future work). Satimage is the low-minority case (9.73%) and Haberman the moderately imbalanced one (26.47%).
irnote: Derived from Table 3: Haberman 225/81 = 2.78; Satimage 5809/626 = 9.28.
specnote: Very small benchmark. Haberman is a small heavily overlapping medical set; Satimage is a larger multiclass set collapsed to one minority class.
prep: Satimage binarised. 10-fold CV, k=5 for all over-samplers, F-value with beta=1. C4.5, Naive Bayes, SVM. Numeric attributes only.
ev: We use two quantitative datasets from UCI Repository of Machine Learning Databases; Satimage and Haberman

title: On Multi-Class Cost-Sensitive Learning (journal version)
ndnote: Identical 20 data sets to the AAAI version; the journal version adds seven cost-sensitive learner types
srcdet: 14 UCI sets and 6 synthetic sets with 2 attributes and 3 or 5 classes.
crit: Same as the conference version. Balanced and imbalanced multi-class sets were chosen to test rescaling with consistent and inconsistent cost matrices. Pure class-imbalance learning is tested on the 10 imbalanced sets. ann is noted as seriously imbalanced, vowel has the most classes, connect4 and splice are large.
irnote: IR not tabulated. Derived as max/min class size: balanced sets 1.0; page 175.5; ann about 40; satellite about 2.5.
specnote: connect4 (67557) gives the large-scale tag. Mixed feature types exist (car, splice, solarflare2) but are not discussed.
prep: Instance weighting, over-sampling, under-sampling, threshold-moving and ensemble variants with C4.5. 10 x 10-fold CV, MAUC.
ev: Twenty multi-class data sets are used in the experiments, where the first 10 data sets are without class-imbalance while the remaining ones are imbalanced.
ds_note: VERIFIED IDENTICAL to the AAAI version: same 20 names, same order, same sizes, attributes, classes and class distributions. The journal extension reuses the conference benchmark unchanged.

title: RAMOBoost: Ranked Minority Oversampling in Boosting
ndnote: 19 real-world datasets; one illustrative synthetic set used only for visualisation
srcdet: UCI plus the ELENA project (Phoneme). Sonar, Spambase, Ionosphere, PID, Wine, German, Vehicle, Texture, Segment, Page_Blocks, Satimage, Mf_Zernike, Vowel, Abalone, Glass, Yeast, Letter, Shuttle.
crit: Stated rationale: the datasets vary in size and class distributions to ensure a thorough assessment of performance. Table I sorts them by degree of skew from nearly balanced (Sonar 0.47:0.53) to extreme (Shuttle 0.001:0.999), so RAMOBoost is tested across a continuum of imbalance, size and dimensionality.
irnote: Derived from Table I: Sonar 111/97 = 1.14; Shuttle 43463/37 about 1175.
specnote: Broadest span of imbalance and size among the early ensemble papers (n from 178 to 43500; IR up to about 1:1175, with only 9 minority samples in Glass and 20 in Yeast). Table II documents explicit minority/majority assignments for every multiclass dataset.
prep: Multiclass converted to binary by explicit class mapping (Vehicle Van vs rest, Satimage damp grey soil, Letter Z vs A-Y, Yeast POX vs CYT). Features nonlinearly normalised to [0,1]. Average of 10 runs with half the data for training. MLP base learner.
ev: The performance of RAMOBoost is evaluated on 19 datasets from the UCI machine learning repository and ELENA project. These datasets vary in size and class distributions

title: RUSBoost: A Hybrid Approach to Alleviating Class Imbalance
ndnote: 15 datasets from several application domains. Table I is now recovered, sorted from the most to the least imbalanced.
srcdet: Three proprietary software-project datasets (SP1, SP3, CCCS12 from Nortel Networks and the US DoD); NASA MDP software-defect sets PC1 and CM1; Mammography; the remainder from UCI (SolarFlareF, Car3, Glass3, Pendigits5, Satimage4, Ecoli4, Segment5, Contra2, Vehicle1).
crit: Chosen to represent a wide variety of dataset sizes, imbalance levels and application domains. Datasets are sorted from most imbalanced (SP3, 1.33% minority) to least (Vehicle1, 25.06%). Multi-class UCI sets were binarised one-vs-rest and continuous-target sets split with a domain-specific threshold.
irnote: The paper reports percentage minority, not IR: 1.33% (SP3) to 25.06% (Vehicle1), which converts to roughly 74.2 down to 2.99.
specnote: Six of the fifteen datasets come from software quality prediction (SP1, SP3, CCCS12, PC1, CM1 and the defect-flavoured CAR3), which is the heaviest software-engineering weighting in the corpus. Three of those are proprietary and were never released, so the benchmark is not fully reproducible. The attribute count includes the dependent attribute.
prep: 10-fold CV repeated 10 times (1500 derived sets). C4.5D, C4.5N, RIPPER, Naive Bayes in Weka; target class distributions 35/50/65%; 10 boosting iterations.
ev: The size of the data sets ranges from 214 examples (Glass3) to 11183 examples (Mammography). The data sets have anywhere from 7 to 43 attributes.

title: Learning from Imbalanced Data in Presence of Noisy and Borderline Examples
ndnote: 9 real datasets (UCI plus the in-house medical set acl) plus 3 families of controlled artificial 2-D datasets at several disturbance levels
srcdet: Real: Acl (authors' medical case studies), Breast cancer, Bupa, Cleveland, Ecoli, Haberman, Hepatitis, New thyroid, Pima. Artificial: two real-valued attributes with minority shapes subclus / clover / paw surrounded by majority.
crit: A controlled analysis of when focused re-sampling beats simple oversampling, so artificial sets are built to vary the borderline/noisy minority fraction (0, 30, 50, 70%), small disjuncts and linear vs non-linear boundaries. Real datasets were reused from the authors' previous SPIDER study and later characterised by PCA plots as separable (acl, new thyroid) or overlapping/noisy (haberman, bupa, pima).
irnote: Artificial sets only: IR 1:3 to 1:9 in a preliminary study; main experiments fix 1:7. Real-set IR not reported.
specnote: Distinctive for synthetic data with explicit control of borderline ratio (0 to 70%), added class noise and minority sub-clusters. Artificial sizes 200 to 1200 generated, 800 used in the main runs.
prep: Artificial: 800 examples, IR 1:7, 5 sub-regions. 10-fold CV repeated 5 times; unpruned C4.5 and MODLEM; HVDM distance for heterogeneous attributes; PCA for 2-D visualisation.
ev: They came either from the UCI repository or from our medical case studies (acl).

title: A dynamic over-sampling procedure based on sensitivity for multi-class problems
ndnote: 12 UCI sets plus 1 real microbiology set (Saureus4). 5 are binary and 8 multi-class. The Drive copy named Static-SMOTE is the same PDF; Static-SMOTE is the static variant defined in section 3.3 of this paper.
srcdet: 12 UCI sets plus Saureus4, a predictive-microbiology dataset (growth/no-growth of Staphylococcus aureus vs temperature, pH, aw; 287 conditions). CYTvsPOX and ME2vsOther derived from Yeast.
crit: The paper states that since the method aims to improve accuracy for the worst classified class when dealing with imbalanced datasets, the datasets selected have a considerable imbalance rate. Binary and multi-class sets with differing instances, features and classes were mixed. Table 3 reports the minimum estimated class prior per dataset, from 0.003 (Yeast) to 0.297.
irnote: IR not reported; paper gives only the minimum prior. Derived from per-class counts of the 8 multi-class sets: Newthyroid 5.0 to Yeast 92.6.
specnote: Mixed feature types (real, binary, nominal). Yeast has a minimum prior of 0.003 (5 of 1484). Five of the 13 datasets are binary, so the paper is mixed binary/multi-class despite the multiclass framing. Evaluation is driven by minimum sensitivity, not by a minority/majority split.
prep: All nominal variables transformed to binary; inputs rescaled to [-2,2]. 10-fold CV with 10 repetitions (Saureus4 uses a fixed split with 30 runs). Correct classification rate and minimum sensitivity.
ev: Since our method is aimed to improve the accuracy for the worst classified class when dealing with imbalanced datasets, the datasets selected have a considerable imbalance rate.

title: Analysing the classification of imbalanced data-sets with multiple classes: Binarization techniques and ad-hoc approaches
authors: Fernandez, Lopez, Galar, del Jesus & Herrera
ndnote: 24 multi-class data sets from the KEEL repository
srcdet: KEEL dataset repository (24 multi-class sets, mostly UCI originals), with KEEL partitions.
crit: A data set is considered imbalanced when one class has less than 40% of the majority class, that is IR > 1.5. The authors justify the selection because the base classifier and plain OVO/OVA get low performance on many of these sets, and note IR alone is not the only difficulty. title: A systematic study of the class imbalance problem in convolutional neural networks
ndnote: MNIST, CIFAR-10 and ILSVRC-2012. Each generates many artificially imbalanced training sets (4050 step + 450 linear for MNIST; 640 networks for CIFAR-10; 5 subsets for ImageNet).

title: Using information on class interrelations to improve classification of multiclass imbalanced data

The four art sets share one profile, two minority classes of 120 and 240 against a majority of 840, and differ only in difficulty. Its dermatology counts sum to 366, the UCI original (doi:10.24432/C5FK5P), not the 358-instance KEEL version used by MC-RBO and MC-NCLWO, and its flare is solar flare 2 with 1389 instances rather than the 1066-instance solar flare 1. title: AB-SMOTE: An Affinitive Borderline SMOTE Approach for Imbalanced Data Binary Classification

title: Combined Cleaning and Resampling Algorithm for Multi-Class Imbalanced Data with Label Noise

title: Radial-Based Oversampling for Multiclass Imbalanced Data Classification

title: Stop Oversampling for Class Imbalance Learning: A Critical Review
ndnote: The authors' own validation uses only Yeast4, Yeast5, Yeast6. Table 1 tabulates, for 72 oversampling methods, the number of datasets used in each original paper.
srcdet: Own experiments: Yeast4, Yeast5, Yeast6 from UCI, each 10 attributes and about 1484 samples (51/44/35 minority).
crit: The 3 datasets were chosen because they are routinely used by many oversampling methods, they are binary, and they stay imbalanced after some majority samples are hidden. The review's central argument is that oversampling is judged only by downstream classification metrics on a few benchmark datasets, with no check that synthesised samples are realistic.
irnote: Computed from Table 2: Yeast4 28.1, Yeast5 32.7, Yeast6 41.4.
specnote: The most directly citable source for criticism of benchmark practice. Its Table 1 lists 72 oversampling methods with the dataset count of each original paper; most use binary data only, the counts have a median of about 9 and a mean of about 12, ranging from 1 to 66, and about 41 of 66 parsed methods used 10 or fewer datasets. It argues that the only methodology for proving an oversampling method's goodness is its classification accuracy after oversampling, with no test of whether the synthetic samples are valid, and reports that all 72 methods produce synthetic samples resembling the majority class. It gives no UCI/KEEL counts and proposes no dataset taxonomy.
prep: Hide 10/25/50% of the majority class at random, oversample, then compare synthetic points to the hidden majority points with Hassanat distance; 5 repeats averaged.
ev: We employ three real-life datasets to put our validation system to the test, namely Yeast4, Yeast5, and Yeast6, which are routinely used by many oversampling methods.

title: Global-local information based oversampling for multi-class imbalanced data

crit: Standard UCI/KEEL multi-class benchmarks with 3 to 11 classes. Instances with missing values were removed, classes with fewer than 10 instances dropped, and class sizes adjusted in some datasets to obtain the required imbalance. Minority classes are not predefined: GLOS identifies them by comparing a class-level discreteness value with instance-level dispersion. specnote: One of the few papers that engineers the class-structure scenario itself: the same source data is re-cut into normal / multi-minority / multi-majority versions. Instance types (Safe / Small Disjunct / Borderline) are analysed per dataset.
prep: Removed missing-value instances; removed classes with fewer than 10 instances; adjusted class sizes in some datasets. C4.5 with OAA/OAO/OAHO/A&O decomposition. 5-fold CV x 10 runs.
ev: 21 multi-class data sets from the UCI repository and KEEL repository are selected. we removed the instances with missing values, removed the classes with less than 10 instances in each data set and adjusted the size of classes in some data sets.

title: Oversampling With Reliably Expanding Minority Class Regions for Imbalanced Data Learning
ndnote: 21 multiclass real-world datasets for OREM-M. The paper also uses 28 two-class UCI datasets for the binary OREM variant, not counted here.
srcdet: Widely used ordinal regression benchmark datasets plus UCI datasets. Examples: Toy, Stock10, Housing10, Abalone, LEV, SWD, Auto5, Voice3/6, Wisconsin5, Vertebral, Cleveland, Dermatology, Page-blocks, Yeast, Plates faults.
crit: Real-world multiclass sets with 3 to 10 classes and varied class-size patterns. Several benchmarks are ordinal-regression sets that were discretised, which gives gradual class-size distributions. The class distribution of every dataset is listed with minority classes in bold. The rebalancing rule oversamples only classes whose imbalance degree exceeds 1.2.
irnote: Overall IR using the SMOM definition, from Table 6 (Vertebral 2.67 to Housing10 152.35).
specnote: Uses a numeric imbalance-degree threshold (1.2) as the operational definition of a minority class, iteratively applied until every class is at or below it. Datasets are uniformly small to medium with no large-scale sets.
prep: Classes oversampled only if imbalance degree > 1.2, iteratively. Macro-F1, MG and MAUC with C4.5, NN and SVM.
ev: 21 multiclass real-world imbalanced datasets are selected for this experiment. They contain widely used ordinal regression benchmark datasets and UCI datasets.

title: GMMSampling: a new model-based, data difficulty-driven resampling method for multi-class imbalanced data
ndnote: 11 real datasets (UCI) plus 4 artificial (Art1-Art4 from the multi-imbalance library). Cleveland_1 and Cleveland_2 are two class-grouping variants of one source.
srcdet: Real data from UCI. Artificial datasets from the multi-imbalance Python toolbox (Grycza et al. 2020). The collection follows the SOUP paper and Lango & Stefanowski 2018.
crit: Datasets were chosen to be diverse: multi-majority, multi-minority and gradual class-size configurations, different class overlap levels and different numbers of classes. The majority/minority labelling per class is taken from the SOUP paper, using two criteria: minority classes must be much smaller than majority ones, and the data-difficulty analysis of example safe levels must show that they are genuinely difficult.
irnote: Paper states IR from 2 to 164, 27.6 on average.
specnote: The clearest statement of a two-criterion minority definition: relative size AND measured example-level difficulty. Within-class subconcepts, overlap and rarity are explicit design targets. Feature counts are not tabulated.
prep: Stratified 5-fold CV averaged over 10 runs. CART, NB, kNN, RF, GBT. Balanced accuracy, macro-F, G-mean, MCC, macro-AP.
ev: including problems with multi-majority, multi-minority, and gradual class size configurations; with different levels of class overlapping and with different numbers of classes, imbalance ratio from 2 to 164 and 27.6 on average.

title: A membership-based resampling and cleaning algorithm for multi-class imbalanced overlapping data
ndnote: 20 real multi-class datasets from UCI and KEEL, plus 60 synthetic two-class datasets (6 IRs x 10 overlap levels) and label noise injected at 0 to 30%

crit: The paper targets class overlap, label noise and data scarcity. The 20 datasets span IR from 1.9 to 853 and 3 to 10 classes with multi-minority and multi-majority distributions. The synthetic sets give controlled IR x overlap grids, and the label-noise experiment randomly replaces labels at 5 to 30%. Minority/majority is determined per class from the class distribution rather than fixed.
irnote: From Table 2 (contraceptive 1.9 to shuttle 853). IR is max/min class size.
specnote: The only multi-class paper here that carries over the binary overlap x IR synthetic grid design. Several sets have tiny classes (ecoli 2/2/5, shuttle 2/6, lymphography 2/4).
prep: 30 x 2-fold CV. RF main classifier (CART, MLP, KNN in the appendix). AvAcc, mean F-measure, CBA and CEN. Label noise added by random label replacement.
ev: Our experiment used 20 multi-class imbalanced datasets from UCI and KEEL repositories.

title: MKC-SMOTE: A Novel Synthetic Oversampling Method for Multi-Class Imbalanced Data Classification
ndnote: 21 real-world multi-class UCI datasets. Table 1 is now recovered. Several are class subsets of the original source (Ecoli 5 of 8 classes, Zoo 5 of 7, Yeast 8 of 10, Letter 10 of 26, Covertype 6 of 7, Abalone 13 classes).
srcdet: UCI repository. Contraceptive Method Choice, User Knowledge Modeling, New-thyroid, Connect-4, Zoo, Cardiotocography, Ecoli, Glass Identification, Absenteeism at Work, Nursery, Letter Recognition, Car Evaluation, Wine Quality-White, Poker Hand, HCV, Yeast, Covertype, Chess (King-Rook vs King), Abalone, Bar Crawl, Avila.
crit: Real, diverse UCI multi-class sets with varying imbalance. A class counts as a minority class if its IR_i = N_max/N_i exceeds 1.45, a threshold taken from a prior thesis to avoid over-oversampling mildly imbalanced classes. Multiple minority and multiple majority classes are handled simultaneously. Five-fold CV is used so every fold contains all classes, because some datasets are small.
irnote: Two measures are reported per dataset. Per-dataset max-over-min IR runs 1.89 (Contraceptive) to 87.47 (Avila). The summed pairwise multi-class IR_overall runs 1.65 (Contraceptive) to 391.52 (Avila) and is not comparable with max-over-min values from other papers. The Car Evaluation row prints 18.91, which its own distribution 1210/384/69/65 does not give; max over min is 18.62, and 1210/64 is 18.91, so the smallest class was probably keyed as 64.

Alongside the usual Ecoli, Glass, Yeast and Zoo it brings in Absenteeism at Work, HCV, Bar Crawl, Avila, Covertype, Poker Hand, Connect-4 and Cardiotocography, none of which appear in the KEEL multi-class suite that the rest of this literature reuses. ev: 21 multi-class imbalanced datasets from the UCI repository were utilized, IR_overall ranging from 1.65 to 391.52 and the IR values ranging from 1.89 to 87.47.
